GET /api/reports/data/m365-inactive-acco.summary: Inactive Microsoft 365 accounts, by client and tenant
GET /api/reports/data/m365-inactive-acco.description: Every account brought in by the Microsoft 365 sync that nobody signs in to, with the client it maps to and the tenant it came from. Options: inactiveDays (default 90, 1–730), includeDisabled and includeUnknown (both default true), tenantId for one connected tenant, plus clientId from the shared report filters. An account with no sign-in activity recorded is reported as unknown rather than inactive, and the payload says so in `notes` — reading it needs Entra ID P1 and AuditLog.Read.All on the app registration. Requires report:view and integration:view.

_README: Curated operation documentation, keyed by `METHOD /path` exactly as the router declares it.
scripts/generate-openapi.mjs merges these into docs/openapi.yaml; anything missing still appears
with a summary derived from its path, so this file is where a description is made *better*, never
where the document is completed. Add an entry when an operation's purpose is not obvious from its
path, when it is what an integrator will reach for, or when its behaviour needs a warning.

POST /api/auth/login.summary: Sign in and receive a session token
POST /api/auth/login.description: Email and password in, a bearer token out. When MFA is enabled the answer is an mfaToken instead, which POST /api/auth/verify-mfa exchanges for the real token. A token is what the Authorization header carries for a person; a program should use an API key instead.

GET /api/auth/me.summary: The signed-in identity, with its permissions
GET /api/auth/me.description: The cheapest way for a client to confirm a credential works and to learn the permissions it holds.

GET /api/auth/client-ip.summary: The address this connection is arriving from
GET /api/auth/client-ip.description: Unauthenticated, because the sign-in screen asks before a session exists and this is the first fact worth having when a sign-in behaves oddly from a VPN, a proxy or a client's network. Answers with the same value the session record and the audit trail carry — `req.ip`, which is the socket address while `trust proxy` is unset — so the screen and the trail agree. Behind a reverse proxy that address is the proxy's until `trust proxy` is configured. Nothing here is instance data: the caller is being handed their own address back.

POST /api/auth/mfa/verify.summary: Exchange an MFA challenge for a session token
POST /api/auth/mfa/verify.description: The second half of MFA sign-in: the mfaToken from POST /api/auth/login plus a TOTP code.

GET /api/api-keys/permissions.summary: Every scope a key may be issued with
GET /api/api-keys/permissions.description: The permission catalogue, so a client can build a key without hard-coding scope names, plus the purposes a key can be labelled with (rmm, siem, flexpoint, quickbooks, monitoring, scheduler, other).

GET /api/api-keys.description: Names, prefixes, scopes, owner, last use and state — never the secret and never its hash. `?includeRevoked=true` keeps the history.

POST /api/api-keys.summary: Issue a key for a program
POST /api/api-keys.description: The only time the secret is returned — store it in the client, and revoke the key if it is lost. The key acts as `userId` (the caller by default), intersected with `permissions`, so it can never exceed the account it borrows.

POST /api/api-keys/:id/rotate.summary: Issue a new secret for the same key
POST /api/api-keys/:id/rotate.description: Scopes, owner and name stay; the previous secret stops working immediately.

DELETE /api/api-keys/:id.description: Recorded as a state rather than a deletion, so the inventory keeps its history. Requests using the key are refused from the next call.

POST /api/events.summary: Receive an event from another system (RMM, SIEM, monitoring)
POST /api/events.description: The gateway every outside system sends to. Idempotent by (source, externalId): a repeat attaches to the ticket the first event opened and counts the occurrence, and `kind: recovery` closes that ticket instead of opening one. Needs ticket:create. Returns what happened — whether a ticket was opened, joined or closed — rather than only that the request was understood.

GET /api/events.summary: Recently received events, with the ticket each became
GET /api/events.description: Filter with ?source= and ?state=open|recovered. Useful for answering "did the RMM reach us?".

GET /api/events/sources.summary: Which systems have sent events, and how many

POST /api/flexpoint/sync.description: Reads customers, invoices and deposits according to the connection's options, stores them, links customers to clients, and records settled payments when that option is on. The same work the Sync button on C7NC → FlexPoint does. A scheduler can call this on a timer: FlexPoint publishes no webhooks, so nothing arrives on its own.

GET /api/flexpoint.summary: The FlexPoint picture: connection, options, counts, client receivables
GET /api/flexpoint.description: Everything the configuration page is drawn from, and the cheapest way to read a client's receivable in bulk.

PUT /api/flexpoint/options.description: What to pull, how customers are matched to clients, whether clients are created for unmatched customers, whether the client id is written back, whether settled payments are recorded, and whether invoices may be pushed. Writes to FlexPoint or to the ledger are off until switched on.

POST /api/flexpoint/link.summary: Tie a FlexPoint customer to a client, or untie it
POST /api/flexpoint/link.description: One customer per client — linking replaces any previous one. `customerId: null` clears the link without touching FlexPoint.

GET /api/flexpoint/clients/:companyId.description: Open balance, overdue, what has been received, the invoices FlexPoint holds, and the FlexPoint payments recorded here.

POST /api/flexpoint/invoices/:invoiceId/.summary: Create or update this invoice in FlexPoint
POST /api/flexpoint/invoices/:invoiceId/.description: Refused unless "push invoices" is switched on for the connection. Idempotent: an invoice that already carries a FlexPoint id is updated rather than created twice.

GET /api/flexpoint/invoices.summary: Local invoices with their FlexPoint state

POST /api/cloudconnect.description: kind, name, credentials and settings. `GET /api/cloudconnect/types` publishes what each connector needs, including the field labels and explanations the configuration dialog shows.

GET /api/cloudconnect/types.description: Every connector kind, what it does, the credentials it needs (with labels, hints and the vendor's own API reference) and the settings it honours.

POST /api/cloudconnect/:id/test.description: A real call to the provider. On failure the answer names the fields at fault and how to fix them.

POST /api/cloudconnect/:id/sync.description: For FlexPoint this runs the full FlexPoint sync (linking and payments included); for every other kind it stores what the adapter returned.

GET /api/cloudconnect/:id/synced-entitie.summary: What a connector has brought in

GET /api/cloudconnect/status.description: State, detail, when it was last verified and whether it is stale, without calling the provider.

POST /api/tickets.description: The same ticket a person would open, with the fields an integrator needs: board, client, contact, priority, assignee. The response carries the `ticketNumber` it was given — `{boardCode}-{client}-{count}`, e.g. `MSP-04-1005`, where the middle part is the client id minus 1000 and the last is that client's ticket count, so it is not a global series and not something to build on: read it back, do not predict it. Prefer POST /api/events for monitoring traffic — it is idempotent, and this is not.

requestExample.title: Printer offline
requestExample.description: Reported by the client's office manager.

GET /api/tickets.description: Filtered and paginated. A client-scoped credential only ever sees its own client's tickets.

PATCH /api/tickets/:id.summary: Update a ticket, including closing it
PATCH /api/tickets/:id.description:
Status, priority, assignment, board and the rest. A status change emails the ticket's contact — that is what the notifications are — so two fields exist to control it. `closeNotes` is the reason the ticket is being closed: it is written to the (customer-visible) thread and it is what the closing email says. `notifyCustomer: false` does the same work in silence, for a ticket whose contact has gone or one closed by mistake.

**Omitting `notifyCustomer` is not the same as sending it**, on a status change that settles the ticket: an absent value means the caller has no opinion and the ticket's board decides, via `notifyCustomerOnClose`. That is how a board whose tickets arrive from monitoring systems at no-reply addresses stays quiet. An explicit `true` or `false` always wins, in both directions.

Closing settles the ticket (`closed`, `resolved`, `cancelled`) and emails the client a message that invites a reply. A reply from one of the client's own contacts reopens the ticket as `customer_reopened` and puts it back in the queue — the reply itself is recorded on the ticket before the status changes.

requestExample.closeNotes: Replaced the failing switch and confirmed the link is stable.

POST /api/tickets/:id/comments.summary: Add a note or reply to a ticket
POST /api/tickets/:id/comments.description: `isInternal: true` keeps the note off the customer's copy, which is what an integration's working notes should be.

GET /api/clients.description: The client list, filterable by status, type, territory and search.

POST /api/clients.description: Only `name` is required. This is what the FlexPoint option "create clients for unmatched customers" calls internally.

POST /api/billing/invoices/generate.summary: Generate an invoice from unbilled time

POST /api/billing/invoices/:id/send.summary: Send an invoice to the client

POST /api/billing/invoices/:id/record-pa.summary: Record a payment against an invoice

POST /api/billing/batches/:id/approve.description: Issues every draft in the batch and offers each invoice to the connected accounting system. When the connection is FlexPoint and pushing is allowed, that push goes through FlexPoint's merchant API.

GET /api/service-alerts.description: What the alert banner and the Outage Board read.

GET /api/alert-webhooks.description: Where this application sends service_alert.raised and service_alert.resolved, with the signing secret and which events each endpoint wants.

POST /api/alert-webhooks/:id/test.summary: Send a test delivery to a webhook

GET /api/console/catalog.summary: The console commands this credential may run
GET /api/console/catalog.description: The command catalogue, grouped the way `help` prints it and filtered by the caller's own permissions at call time, so a client is told what *it* can run rather than shipped a list it will be refused. Every command names the route it runs and the permission that route checks; the console itself has no permission, and authorizes nothing — it builds the same request the screen builds and lets the route decide (PLAN-028 §6). Reads only: the write commands arrive with PLAN-026's action manifest. `counts.total` is reported beside `counts.available` so a caller can see what its account is missing without being told what it contains. Answers 404 when the console is switched off for the deployment.

GET /api/console/catalog/:name.summary: One console command, with its flags and its route
GET /api/console/catalog/:name.description: A single descriptor, for `c7ntax help <command>` and for tooling. The name is the command as typed (`ticket show`), so it is URL-encoded; `+` is accepted for the space. A command the caller's credential may not run is 404, not 403: the catalogue is filtered rather than guarded, and not being offered a command is indistinguishable from it not existing — which is the same rule the record lookups follow.

GET /api/alert-webhooks/deliveries.summary: What was delivered, and what failed

GET /api/system/changelog.summary: What's New — the release notes as structured data

GET /api/system/version.summary: The version the running build identifies as
GET /api/system/version.description: The newest entry of the same notes `/changelog` returns, without the change history: for labelling the application itself — the account menu shows the build beside the logo — and for answering "what is this deployment running?" in one request. Parsed once and re-read only when BuildNotes.md changes, so the label costs nothing per page load. `version`, `date` and `title` are null on a build whose notes cannot be read, rather than a 404: an unknown version is a state a client can render, not an error worth logging.

GET /api/system/audit-logs.description:
Actions with their actor, entity and timestamp. This is the join an SIEM wants: correlate a detection with the change someone made after it.

Two optional filters, both of which only narrow the result. `mine=true` limits the rows to the caller's own — narrower than the unfiltered read this route has always served, and what the header's Recent activity menu asks for, so a caller is never shown a colleague's activity under the word "mine". `limit` caps the page (default 500, maximum 500): the audit screen wants hundreds of rows and a menu wants five.

`entityId` is the record the action touched where the route had one. For a creation that is the id of the row the route returned, so a created record can be linked to; for a route with no id in its path it is the last path segment, which for a collection is the collection's name (`clients`) and for an action is the action (`generate`) — so a client reading this should treat a non-id `entityId` as "the operation or the collection", not as a record.

GET /api/configuration.description: Every setting the application reads: value, source (default, environment, or saved), what changing it affects, and what it defaults to.

GET /api/portal/tickets.summary: The customer portal's own ticket list
GET /api/portal/tickets.description: Portal routes are authenticated by a contact's one-time code, not by a staff session — they are listed here so the surface is complete, not as something an integration should call.

GET /api/kb.description: The published articles, with /api/kb/drafts for the ones not published and /api/kb/categories for the tree.

GET /api/reports/:id/run.summary: Run a report and get its rows
GET /api/reports/:id/run.description: The custom report designer's runner: a stored template rendered against live data, returning the rows and the totals it computed.

GET /api/dashboard/layout.description: Per-user, not global: this is the arrangement of the widgets on the caller's own dashboard.

GET /api/oauth-app.summary: What the OAuth app wizard needs before it starts
GET /api/oauth-app.description: The permissions a deployment will request (`Mail.ReadWrite` as an application role, `Mail.ReadWrite`/`User.Read`/`offline_access` delegated), the redirect URI this instance must be registered with for the delegated flow, the default registration name, and the by-hand command that does the same thing from a terminal. `integration:manage`.

POST /api/oauth-app/start.summary: Begin a deployment: a device code for the tenant administrator
POST /api/oauth-app/start.description: Starts the OAuth device-code flow against Microsoft's public Graph command-line client, so nothing about the tenant is held here and the administrator signs in themselves. Returns the code to type and the URL to open; poll the session until it is authorised. The tenant may be a GUID or a primary domain, and a tenant that does not exist is refused by name.

POST /api/oauth-app/import.summary: Read the script's output (or the four values) instead of deploying from here
POST /api/oauth-app/import.description: The offline path through the wizard, for a tenant this instance cannot reach the Microsoft sign-in endpoint, or a registration that already exists. Paste the contents of `O365/out/c7ntax-m365-app.json` in `scriptJson`, or send `tenantId`/`clientId`/`clientSecret`/`mailbox` directly. Refuses a client id that is not a GUID, and refuses a registration granted `Mail.Read` instead of `Mail.ReadWrite` — the connector marks messages read, so read-only connects and then fails on the first message.

warnings: Confirm the Exchange Online scoping commands were run: until they are, an app-only registration can read every mailbox in the tenant.

POST /api/oauth-app/:sessionId/poll.summary: Has the administrator approved the sign-in yet?
POST /api/oauth-app/:sessionId/poll.description: Asks Microsoft. Answers `pending` while the code is unapproved (and lengthens the interval if Microsoft says `slow_down`), `authorized` once a token has been granted — with the account and tenant id read from that token's claims — or `declined`/`expired` with the reason. Deploying before this says `authorized` is refused with 409.

POST /api/oauth-app/:sessionId/deploy.summary: Create or reuse the registration, grant consent, mint the secret
POST /api/oauth-app/:sessionId/deploy.description: The same sequence as `O365/New-C7NTAXMailboxApp.ps1`, over Graph: find or create the application by display name (an existing one is *reused*, not duplicated), record `requiredResourceAccess` with the application role id of `Mail.ReadWrite` (and the delegated scope ids plus the redirect URI when the delegated flow is wanted), create the service principal consent is granted *to*, grant admin consent with all three ids, and create a client secret for 12 months unless the flow is delegated (which uses PKCE and must not have one). Also returns the Exchange Online commands that scope an app-only registration to one mailbox — Graph has no route to those. The secret is returned once and never stored by this API; the audit row keeps the expiry instead.

warnings: Confirm the Exchange Online scoping commands were run: until they are, an app-only registration can read every mailbox in the tenant.

GET /api/oauth-app/:sessionId.summary: Where a deployment got to, without contacting Microsoft
GET /api/oauth-app/:sessionId.description: The session's own state: pending, authorized, declined, expired or failed, plus the tenant, mode, mailbox and display name it was started with.

POST /api/tickets/batch.summary: Apply one change to many tickets
POST /api/tickets/batch.description:
Status and priority only. `notifyCustomer: false` closes a batch without emailing anybody, which is usually what housekeeping wants; `closeNotes` is recorded on every ticket in the batch. Note that closing a batch *does* email each ticket's contact, one ticket at a time — there is no digest.

Omit `notifyCustomer` and the board decides **per ticket**, because a single selection can span boards: a NOC ticket stays quiet while the ones beside it are told. Send `true` or `false` and that answer is used for all of them.

In the application, a batch that includes **Close** stops and asks first (email the client, or close in silence) rather than closing in the background: the request below is what that dialog sends, not what a ticked checkbox sends on its own.

GET /api/procurement/orders.description: Filtered by `status` and `vendorId`, newest first, with each order's vendor and lines included. Nothing here is client-scoped: a purchase order is ours, not a customer's.

GET /api/procurement/orders/:id.description: The record rather than the row: the lines as ordered (with the catalog SKU where a line came from the catalog), the vendor's own details, who raised and who approved it, and the four dates that say whether it is late — created, ordered, expected, received.

POST /api/procurement/orders.description: `vendorId` is required and the number is generated (`PO-?`). Totals are computed from the lines, so `subtotal` sent by a caller is ignored.

PATCH /api/procurement/orders/:id.summary: Move a purchase order along, or re-price it before it arrives
PATCH /api/procurement/orders/:id.description:
`status` is one of `draft`, `ordered`, `shipped`, `received`; moving to `ordered` stamps `orderedAt` and moving to `received` stamps `receivedAt` unless a date is sent, so a late delivery can be recorded as the day it actually arrived. `expectedAt` and `notes` are editable at any point.

**Receiving an order writes the asset inventory**: one asset per unit, named from the line, tagged `{poNumber}-{line}-{unit}`, priced at the line's cost and carrying the order number, unassigned until somebody puts it at a client. The reply's `assets.created` says how many were written; one line is capped at 25 records and the remainder is added to the order's notes rather than dropped; re-receiving the same order writes nothing twice.

`lineItems` replaces the lines and recomputes `subtotal` and `total` from them — refused once the order is `received`, because a receipt is a record of what arrived and a line list that can change afterwards is not one. A status moved back from `received` clears `receivedAt`.

PATCH /api/procurement/vendors/:id.description: The details that end up on a purchase order: who to contact, how to reach them, the payment terms that decide when their invoice is due, and the tax id it has to match.
